stride_test.formula: sigma_k = 1.4826 * MAD(p(f+k) - 2p(f) + p(f-k)) / sqrt(6), per axis, rows of one track at f-k, f, f+k
stride_test.interpretation: sigma_k grows with k (about 1.1 px at k=1 to about 2.5-3.2 px at k=8), so the second differences are not pure white noise. If all of the k=8 spread were locally constant acceleration over 16 frames, its share at k=1 would be at most sigma_8/64 (about 0.04-0.05 px), far below the observed k=1 spread (about 1.1 px). Under that assumption most of the frame-to-frame second difference is not smooth motion: detector box jitter and/or high-frequency image motion such as camera vibration (which is real image motion, not detector error). The assumption fails for abrupt motion, so this is evidence, not an isolation of noise from movement.
